# Add an action or a check

A page has one class per door, in `pages/<type>/actions/`. Each has a YOURS block for its methods:

| Door | Class | Method returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click()` | `...ClickActions` | the next page if the click changes page, else `this` |
| `enter()` | `...EnterActions` | `this` |
| `check()` / `uncheck()` | `...CheckActions` | `this` (one method serves both: it gets `check`) |
| `clear()` | `...ClearActions` | `this` |
| `read()` | `...ReadActions` | the value |
| `verify()` | `...VerifyActions` | `this` |
| `execute()` | `...Tasks` | a sequence of steps a story names, one method each (add-a-task.md) |
| `navigateTo()` | `HeaderNavigableActions` (the header and footer) | the page the menu link leads to, from any page |

Name each method for what a visitor does or sees (`signUp()`, `email(text)`, `showsThanks()`),
never for the element's technology (`clickButton2()`). Build it from the library, one line:

```java
    public SiteDetail2ClickActions acceptTerms() {
        UserActions.click(page, SiteDetail2Elements.ACCEPT_BUTTON);
        return this;
    }

    /** Sends the form; the thank-you page comes next. */
    public ThanksPage submit() {
        UserActions.click(page, SiteDetail2Elements.SUBMIT_BUTTON);
        return new ThanksPage(page).get();
    }

    public SiteDetail2VerifyActions showsThanks() {
        Checks.isShown(page, SiteDetail2Elements.THANKS_HEADING);
        return this;
    }
```

The library logs each step in plain English and waits for the element. When nothing in it fits,
log the step yourself with `StepLog.step("...")` before doing it, and wait with `WaitActions`,
never `Thread.sleep`. A click that leads to another page returns `new NextPage(page).get()`,
which waits until that page has fully loaded; import that page class in the file's **imports**
YOURS block (`import com.xoveconsulting.tests.pages.<type>.NextPage;`) if the file does not import it already.

Every verify() already has `shows(element)`, `doesNotShow(element)`, `says(element, text)` and
`showsText(text)`. Add a named check when the story's words say more than that (`showsThanks()`
reads better than `shows(SiteDetail2Elements.THANKS_HEADING)`).
